summary: Jesus withdraws beyond the Jordan to the place where John first baptized, and many come to Him and believe, saying all John said about Him was true.
key_insight: The people’s verdict on John the Baptist was simple: “John performed no sign, but all the things that John spoke about this Man were true.” John never worked a miracle, yet after his death his true words led many to believe, at the very place he had preached.
story: After the Feast of Dedication, Jesus left Jerusalem and went away again beyond the Jordan, to the place where John had been baptizing at first. There He stayed.
Many people came to Him there. They said, “John performed no sign, but all the things that John spoke about this Man were true.”
And many believed in Him there.

scene.label: Back where it began
scene.text: John 1:28 places John’s first baptizing at Bethabara beyond the Jordan (most Greek manuscripts read Bethany beyond the Jordan, a different place from the Bethany of Martha and Mary). There John had pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God, and there Jesus’ first disciples began to follow Him (John 1:29–42).

scene.label: Beyond the Jordan
scene.text: The land east of the Jordan, called Perea, was ruled by Herod Antipas, not by Pilate or the Jerusalem leaders. It put distance between Jesus and those who had just tried to stone Him.

scene.label: No sign
scene.text: The Gospels record no miracle by John the Baptist. His work was to point away from himself: “He must increase, but I must decrease” (John 3:30).

witnesses.john: Only John records this quiet stay. It brings Jesus’ public ministry back to where John’s Gospel first showed it, beside the Baptist’s witness (1:19–34), and it closes the long account of conflict in Jerusalem with a note of faith. Here, it seems, the message about Lazarus will reach Him (11:3–6).

seeing.reveals: Rejected in the temple, Jesus is welcomed by ordinary people by the river. The One John pointed to is exactly who John said He was.
seeing.living: John’s work outlived him because it pointed away from himself. You may never work a sign, but true words about Jesus, faithfully spoken, can bear fruit long after you have said them.
seeing.ponder: If people weighed your words about Jesus after you were gone, would they find them true?

preaching.big_idea: A faithful witness to Jesus bears fruit long after the witness is gone.
preaching.watch_for: The word “many” comes twice (vv. 41–42), right after the stones of 10:31 and the attempt to seize Him in 10:39. John sets the welcome by the Jordan against the rejection in the temple.

title: Withdrawing Beyond the Jordan
